Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Labour Party Manifesto 2005: Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision and record
- Purpose: “Forward, not back” – government’s duty is to provide opportunity and security for all, marrying economic dynamism with social justice and matching rights with responsibilities.
- Record since 1997: Longest period of growth; lowest unemployment/inflation for a generation; 2m more in work; minimum wage and tax credits raised living standards; poverty among children and pensioners reduced. Major investment in schools and NHS (more teachers, doctors, nurses; faster treatments; heart and cancer deaths down). Crime down ~30% with more police and new community powers. Aid doubled and UK leading on climate policy.

Economy and enterprise
- Maintain macro stability: 2% inflation target, fiscal rules, low debt; no rise in basic/top income tax; no VAT on essentials; efficiency savings to fund services.
- Jobs and skills: Target 80% employment; higher minimum wage; welfare-to-work and Incapacity Benefit reform; expand apprenticeships and FE; science/innovation strategy to lift R&D to 2.5% of GDP by 2014.
- Business and infrastructure: Competitive taxation; lighter, better regulation; support SMEs and entrepreneurship; £180bn+ public transport investment to 2015; rail upgrades, HS options, congestion solutions (incl. road pricing study); free off-peak bus travel for over-60s.

Education
- Personalised learning: More teachers/support staff; parental engagement; firm discipline.
- Primary: Sustain literacy/numeracy gains; enrich arts, sport, languages; upgrade buildings.
- Secondary: All schools to be independent specialist schools; at least 200 Academies by 2010; Building Schools for the Future modernises estates; expansion where demand/quality justify.
- 14–19: Strengthen vocational routes with specialised diplomas; EMAs; more apprenticeships/FE.
- Higher education: More places with variable fees capped at £3,000, grants and bursaries; aim 50% participation; research investment boosted.

Health and social care
- NHS investment to triple by 2008; referral-to-treatment max 18 weeks; patient choice of hospital; expand primary/community services and community hospitals; prudent use of independent sector for capacity; cut bureaucracy; tackle MRSA and improve hygiene; dentistry review.
- Public health: Better school meals, nutrition standards and labelling; restrict junk-food marketing to children; smoke-free workplaces/restaurants (limited exemptions); expand cessation services; health trainers.

Crime, security, migration
- Neighbourhood policing in every community; more CSOs; strong action on antisocial behaviour and alcohol-related disorder; youth justice reforms.
- Cut drug-driven crime with compulsory testing/treatment; new Serious Organised Crime Agency.
- Tougher gun/knife controls; reduce reoffending with supervision, tagging, NOMS.
- Victim-focused justice; corporate manslaughter law; ID cards to combat fraud/illegal working.
- Immigration: Points system favouring skills; English for settlement; biometric visas/e-passports; employer penalties; faster, fair asylum.

Families, housing, older people
- Halve child poverty by 2010 and end it in a generation via work, tax credits, Child Trust Fund.
- Universal childcare: Sure Start Children’s Centres nationwide; extended schools 8am–6pm; more help with childcare costs.
- Parental leave to nine months (aim a year); expand flexible working (including carers).
- Housing: Increase homeownership by up to 2m; raise stamp duty threshold; shared-ownership/right-to-buy style schemes; more and better social housing with choice-based lettings.
- Older people: Pension Credit; Winter Fuel Payments; free local bus travel; forge consensus on long-term pensions; end unjustified forced retirement before 65; individual care budgets.

International, environment, culture, democracy
- Europe: Lead reform; referendum on Constitutional Treaty; NATO central; euro only if tests met.
- Security and development: Counter terrorism/WMD; support Iraq/Afghanistan transitions; Middle East peace; maintain nuclear deterrent; UN/G8 leadership on Africa and climate; reach 0.7% ODA by 2013; fairer trade.
- Environment: Clean neighbourhoods, higher recycling, brownfield building, sustainable homes, Marine Act; long-term CO2 cuts (−20% by 2010; −60% by 2050).
- Culture/sport: Free national museums; broaden participation; facility upgrades; 2012 Olympics legacy; BBC Trust and digital switchover 2008–2012.
- Democracy: More neighbourhood powers; stronger, freer local government; mayoral options; council tax restraint; further devolution; complete Lords reform; Single Equality Act and Equality & Human Rights Commission.

TEXT_F:
Conservative Party Manifesto 2005 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core message: Britain has great potential but is heading in the wrong direction under Labour. The Conservatives promise action over talk, rewarding hard work, restoring accountability, devolving power, and focusing on practical priorities: cleaner hospitals, school discipline, more police, controlled immigration and lower taxes.

Economy and tax:
- Cut waste and borrowing to fund tax cuts: save £12bn/year by 2007–08 (civil service freeze, 235,000 fewer bureaucratic posts, scrap/merge 168 bodies); use £8bn to reduce borrowing and £4bn for tax cuts.
- Lower, simpler taxes to promote work and enterprise; keep minimum wage and planned rises.
- Halve council tax bills (up to £500) for households where all residents are over 65, funded centrally.
- Pensions: restore earnings link for the basic state pension; keep Winter Fuel Payment, over-75 TV licences, and 2005 council tax payment. Create Lifetime Savings Accounts; strengthen workplace pensions (opt-out schemes); use unclaimed financial assets to protect failed scheme members.
- Stability: keep Bank of England independence; no to the Euro. Deregulation via regulatory budgets, sunset reviews, end EU “gold-plating”; restore UK opt-out from EU Social Chapter.

Education and families:
- Flexible childcare: more flexible maternity pay; up to £50/week per under-5 via Working Tax Credit for all qualifying working families, usable for formal or informal care; support workplace nurseries and after-school clubs.
- Restore discipline: give heads/governors full control over admissions/expulsions; Turnaround Schools for disruptive pupils; protect teachers from malicious allegations; slash paperwork; funding to follow the pupil.
- Raise standards: scrap grade-inflation targets; publish marks alongside grades; allow international qualifications; slim and depoliticise the National Curriculum; 300,000 vocational grants for 14–16s; more sport (two hours after-school) and ban junk food in schools.
- Higher/further education: scrap university tuition fees; abolish the admissions regulator; build endowments; simplify FE funding and empower “super colleges.”

NHS and social care:
- Increase NHS funding by £34bn over the Parliament; shift power to professionals; abolish Strategic Health Authorities, cut PCTs and quangos; end central targets; funding to follow patients; more single rooms and infection control; restore matrons with power to close wards; protect community hospitals.
- End waiting lists as we know them; offer NHS contribution (half NHS cost) for self-pay operations to cut queues.
- Reform dentistry (low monthly payment option); more support for carers; partnership scheme so no one must sell their home for long-term care.
- Health checks for long-stay non-EU migrants; STI public health campaign.

Crime and security:
- 5,000 extra police officers each year; slash paperwork; elected police commissioners; genuine neighbourhood policing.
- 20,000 extra prison places; end early release; honesty in sentencing.
- Drugs: 25,000 residential rehab places; hard-drug users: treatment or court; reclassify cannabis to Class B.
- Appoint a Homeland Security Minister; robust counter-terror measures.

Immigration and borders:
- Controlled immigration with popular consent: 24/7 port surveillance, restored embarkation controls, create a British Border Control Police.
- Australian-style points system prioritising needed skills.
- Asylum: repatriate powers from the EU; replace the 1951 Geneva framework with modern agreements; process claims outside the UK; fixed annual refugee quota via UNHCR; overall annual immigration limit set by Parliament.

Constitution, communities, and environment:
- Accountability: Timetable for Action; ministers who fail will go. Abolish regional assemblies; strengthen Parliament and select committees; cut MPs by 20%; English votes for English laws.
- Devolution: back the Union; Welsh referendum on Assembly powers; stricter standards for NI executive participation.
- Localism: devolve planning/housing/transport/fire to councils; tougher action on illegal traveller camps; devolve arts and Lottery decisions.
- Housing: extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership.
- Transport: end “war on motorists”; modernise roads; review all speed cameras; longer rail franchises.
- Environment: protect Green Belt, prioritise brownfield; phase out HFCs; lower VED for low-emission cars; boost home energy efficiency; expand renewables and energy security; more recycling.
- Rural/agriculture: honest food labelling; require Little Red Tractor in public procurement; push CAP reform; strengthen animal welfare; free vote to overturn hunting ban.

Foreign policy and defence:
- Spend £2.7bn more on the military front line by 2007–08; preserve regiments and warships; NATO at the core; support service families.
- Iraq: stay to rebuild and support democracy; pursue Middle East peace (secure Israel and viable Palestinian state).
- Europe: oppose EU Constitution (referendum within six months); no Euro; restore Social Chapter opt-out; repatriate fisheries control; back enlargement including Turkey.
- Aid: meet 0.7% of GNI by 2013; increase UK control of aid; champion open markets, rule of law and property rights.

First-month actions: begin recruiting 5,000 extra police per year; restore matrons; first Budget to cut waste and lower taxes; empower heads to expel; start 24/7 port surveillance; set date for EU Constitution referendum (campaign for No).
